title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure whether a deterministic validator plus one allowed automated repair could reduce executable unsafe LLM‑generated network configurations relative to reusing the identical sampled candidate without repair (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on N = 200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared initial candidate passed validation so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We report artifact‑grounded methodology, representative validator diagnostics, execution accounting, and concrete preregistered follow‑on estimand changes required to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling, higher difficulty, or adversarial conditions.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are proposed for intent→configuration translation in network operations (NetOps). However, unconstrained LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, logically inconsistent command sequences, or fabricated fields that, if executed, violate redundancy or availability requirements. A natural architecture to mitigate those risks is generate→validate→repair (GVR): produce a candidate configuration, apply deterministic validation checks that assess executability and policy constraints, and optionally trigger automated repair. Prior work shows verifier‑guided feedback can reduce incorrect artifacts in related domains (e.g., IaC and program repair), but the transfer of those gains to device‑level NetOps execution remains an open empirical question in the verified literature [3].

This paper reports a fully preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment that evaluated the downstream effect of a deterministic validator and a permitted single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under these semantics any paired difference must arise solely from validator‑triggered repair applied to the identical candidate; sampling variability between conditions is by design excluded. Our contributions are: (1) an artifact‑grounded report of the executed paired experiment (N = 200 pairs) with validator traces and provider audit data; (2) exact confirmatory inferential results for the executed estimand showing no discordant pairs and a degenerate null effect; and (3) explicit, artifact‑grounded recommendations and preregistered follow‑on estimand changes required to evaluate repair efficacy when independent sampling or adversarial task uplift are introduced.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and reliability problems for LLMs are widely documented and motivate grounding and verification strategies in operational contexts [1]. Retrieval‑ and evidence‑grounded pipelines have reduced hallucination in operations‑style QA tasks, though such work typically evaluates textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulators [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures (for example, verifier‑guided IaC repair systems) report empirical correctness improvements in adjacent domains and therefore motivate analogous NetOps pipelines; however, the supplied verified records do not contain standardized execution‑level evaluations on packet‑level network simulations or device emulators that measure end‑to‑end safety [3].

NetOps LLM evaluations exist that assess translation accuracy and capability, but a consistent execution‑level safety benchmark in packet‑level simulation is not present among the verified corpus and thus motivated our confirmatory design [4]. Our study is deliberately narrow and methodological: it isolates the validator/repair causal effect on a fixed sampled candidate (shared_initial_candidate), rather than conflating that effect with generation‑time sampling or prompt engineering.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01 before any model calls. The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Design parameters from the preregistration: task_count = 200 paired intents, planned_episode_count = 400, maximum_model_calls = 400, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two‑sided McNemar test; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) supplements inference. Missingness policy used complete_pair_primary (exclude incomplete pairs); sensitivity analyses treating missing/failed episodes as failures were preregistered but not required because none occurred.

Task bank, contamination checks, and selection. A deterministic task generator produced the fixed manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks. Each manifest entry included an initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotation (e.g., "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and generation_seed for deterministic replay. Prior to model calls the preregistered contamination checks (SHA‑256 exact‑match and n‑gram similarity thresholds) were executed and flagged no exact‑match leaks; the confirmatory sample remained intact. Representative manifest fields and difficulty annotations are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution adhered strictly to shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted adapter labeled openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic sampling remains possible. Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with a single shared generation per pair.

Validator and repair pipeline. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation". The validator produced binary executable/invalid labels and structured traces (validation_before/validation_after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). Guarded episodes were allowed at most one automated repair attempt (preregistered); under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline episodes reused the same sampled candidate without repair. All per‑episode validator traces and repair metadata were archived (execution/scoring/*.json).

Statistical analysis. The preregistered primary test was the exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 paired contingency table. We computed exact p‑values and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) for the paired difference. All quantities reported below are computed from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv). Deterministic reconciliation and provider audit artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) were used to verify sample and call accounting.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200, and completed_pair_count = 200. The provider audit summary (deterministic reconciliation) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, confirming one shared generation per pair.

Primary outcomes and inferential results. The per‑condition summaries are baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table observed guarded vs baseline: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. These analytic artifacts are archived under analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 because no shared initial candidate triggered a validator violation. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json and task‑000004‑guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate text and identical validation_after.normalized_configuration values for both baseline and guarded. Example (task‑000004 shared initial candidate excerpt):

interface edge2 admin down
interface edge2 vlan 40
interface edge2 admin up
interface edge1 admin down

For that example parsed_command_count = 4 and required_command_count = 4 and validator.valid = true. Representative diagnostics for other hard tasks (task‑000005, task‑000006) are archived and summarized in Table 2.

Contamination, reconciliation, and archival evidence. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact‑match leaks; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and reports cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. Key archived artifacts enabling independent verification include execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/scoring/*.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt. These artifacts and their hashes are present in the evidence bundle for independent reanalysis.

Compact result summary (artifact‑grounded). Table 1 presents the 2×2 paired contingency counts and primary statistics. Table 3 explicitly records repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 so the causal pathway leading to the degenerate null effect is immediately visible.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation within the executed estimand. The preregistered estimand measured only the downstream effect of deterministic validation and a permitted single automated repair on the identical sampled candidate per intent. Because every sampled candidate was validator‑valid, the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to apply repairs and could not change outcomes; the degenerate contingency table (zero discordant pairs) is therefore an artifact‑grounded finding about the executed estimand rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.

Threats to validity and construct limits. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally eliminate sampling variability; this preserves a clean causal contrast for downstream validator/repair but restricts any claim to that narrow causal object. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mapped intent constraints (syntax, sequence constraints, protected interfaces) but does not perform vendor‑specific CLI execution or packet‑level runtime emulation. Thus some failure modes (timing, protocol interactions, real device idiosyncrasies) are outside the validator’s abstraction.

External and conclusion validity. External validity is limited by a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter), a synthetic deterministic task bank, and a single validator implementation. Conclusion validity: with zero discordant pairs no inferential evidence about repair efficacy under independent per‑condition sampling can be drawn; any affirmative claim about repair benefits under broader sampling requires a different preregistered estimand and a task distribution with a higher expected validator failure rate.

Operational implications and recommended preregistered follow‑ons (artifact‑grounded). The archived pipeline supports several precise follow‑on preregistered experiments that change the estimand and are therefore new confirmatory tests: (A) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics to produce independent first‑pass generations per arm so repair can act on a broader set of validator‑detectable faults; (B) sample targeted high‑difficulty or adversarial task subsets from the manifest (difficulty = "extreme") to raise expected validator failure rates; (C) set explicit numeric temperatures in model_configuration.json and preregister temperature sweeps to quantify diversity vs validator‑failure tradeoffs; (D) increase validator fidelity by integrating vendor CLI semantics or packet‑level emulation before scoring; (E) expand to multi‑model sampling to probe generality. Each recommended change is directly supported by the archived artifacts and by the preregistration metadata describing planned estimand modifications.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that measured the downstream effect of deterministic validation and a permitted single automated repair on the identical sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). With gpt‑5‑mini as the declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the scorer, all sampled candidates passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical for the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This narrow, artifact‑grounded result demonstrates that under the sampled tasks and shared_initial_candidate design there was no opportunity for repair to change outcomes; it does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary in general. Concretely: the executed estimand isolated validator/repair effect on a fixed sampled candidate; independent per‑condition sampling or adversarial task uplift are required (and preregistered) to empirically evaluate repair effectiveness in practice. Table 3 restates repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 to make this degenerate pathway explicit. The archived artifacts support independent verification and provide a foundation for the preregistered follow‑on estimands described above.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
